subject: Evaluating sub-ledger & subscription billing vendors — scope, timelines, next steps
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightbill.co>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: netsuite-sales@oracle.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: BrightBill interest — trial & integration notes

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As promised, I'm sending a short summary of how BrightBill typically works for companies doing high-touch subscriptions + sub-ledger requirements. Attached: a one-page proposal and integration checklist.

Quick highlights:
- Native support for complex billing events (prorations, credit memos, tiered usage).
- Sub-ledger export that maps cleanly into NetSuite (we provide a transform layer).
- Sandbox for realistic replay of last 30 days of billing events.

If it helps, we can stand up a two-week pilot (sandbox + test invoice run) for Redwood so your finance team can validate mappings and reconciliation. Typical pilot scope: 1) sample migration of AR history (30 days), 2) 3 end-to-end billing scenarios, 3) reconciliation report.

Available demo slots next week: Tue/Wed mornings PT. Let me know what works and I'll send calendar invites + a short agenda.

Best,
Sam
Head of Sales Engineering | BrightBill
A: BrightBill-proposal.pdf (attached)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBill interest — trial & integration notes

Team — looping you in. Summary below and suggested next steps.

Summary from Sam: BrightBill can do sub-ledger exports that map to NetSuite, plus a sandbox and a pilot run. They propose a 2-week pilot.

Why we're evaluating: our current billing provider has limited event modeling (makes refunds and credit memos messy) and reconciliation with NetSuite is manual. We need to reduce month-end adjustments and speed up invoice ops.

Suggested next steps:
- Confirm pilot objectives (Marissa) — what minimal data we need to validate for month-end accounting.
- Legal/procurement check: what contract term & SOW review (Michael).
- Technical: quick engineering spot-check for sandbox access and replay (Laura).

Availability: I can join a vendor demo Wed 14 Jul 09:30 PT or Thu 15 Jul 10:00 PT. If those don't work, propose alternatives.

Please reply with priorities and any must-have questions for the vendor (integration, SLAs, data retention, support model).

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBill interest — trial & integration notes

Evelyn — thanks for the summary. For the pilot objectives I propose the following minimal acceptance criteria:

1) Invoice parity: for a sample of 1,000 invoices, BrightBill-generated invoices must match our current system on 99.5% of line-level charge calculations.
2) Reconciliation: automated GL posting to NetSuite with no manual adjustments needed for the sample run (or clearly documented exceptions).
3) Refunds/credit memos: correct mapping to NetSuite credit memos and minimal bolt-on scripts.
4) SLA: vendor support response time within 2 business hours during pilot incidents.

Also add data retention policy and encryption-at-rest confirmation to the checklist.

I'll start a short eval matrix and attach it for the demo — includes fields for feature checks, integration effort (low/med/high), preliminary cost buckets.

Marissa
Director, Finance Systems | Redwood Inference
Attachment: billing-eval-matrix.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBill interest — trial & integration notes

Evelyn/Marissa — a couple of technical notes to add to the pilot scope from the infra side:

- NetSuite connectivity: we need to validate both the GL mapping and the subsidiary/segment mapping (we run multiple legal entities). BrightBill's transform layer must allow per-subsidiary rules.
- Keys & secrets: vendor must support our KMS pattern or provide HSM options; no long-term credentials stored in plaintext.
- Latency & webhook delivery: we need to simulate peak billing spikes (monthly close) to measure webhook/backfill throughput.

Also, NetSuite licensing can be a blocker if the vendor requires additional connector modules — please confirm with Sam whether their export uses standard SuiteTalk APIs only or requires SuiteCloud connectors. Sam, can you clarify?

Thanks,
Laura
Engineering Manager, Platform Integrations
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@brightbill.co>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBill interest — trial & integration notes

Thanks for the questions — quick answers inline and next steps.

Laura: BrightBill uses SuiteTalk REST/SOAP endpoints and our standard export doesn't require buyer-side SuiteCloud connectors. We map by subsidiary code and support custom segment transforms during pilot.

Marissa: We'll include the data retention and encryption details in the pilot SOW. Response SLA for pilot incidents: 1 business hour for severity 1, 4 hours for severity 2.

Evelyn: Confirming we can start a two-week sandbox pilot starting Mon 20 Jul. For the pilot we'll need:
- API creds for sandbox NetSuite account (read/write for staging subsidiary)
- Sample dataset (can be an anonymized 30-day export)
- 2 vendor/Redwood leads for daily sync (15 min)

I've attached the short proposal and our SOW template for procurement review. If that all looks good I'll send calendar invites for the kickoff (20 Jul 10:00 PT) and the demo.

Attachments: BrightBill-proposal.pdf, SOW-template.docx

Best,
Sam
